lines.differs: Tougher on AtliQ than Al Noor: absolute exclusivity requirement for all professional time, instead of just restricting data analytics services within the GCC.
Tougher on AtliQ than CloudSpan: total service exclusivity versus only restricting activity as an implementation or referral partner for competing cloud platforms.
Tougher on AtliQ than Orbit Travels: restricts all professional work for any third party instead of only prohibiting travel-booking software development in India.
Tougher on AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: payment term is 60 days after approval instead of 30 days after receipt of invoice.
Tougher on AtliQ than Trustline NBFC: payment takes 60 days from approval instead of 45 days from receipt, and approval is at client's discretion.
Tougher on AtliQ than PayTrack: 60-day payment term following timesheet approval compared to a 30-day term following invoice receipt.
Tougher on AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: client owns all work product and IP upon creation, whereas Rohan Iyer allowed the contractor to retain ownership.
Tougher on AtliQ than Al Noor: ownership vests upon creation rather than after full payment, with no explicit reservation for AtliQ's background IP.
Tougher on AtliQ than Orbit Travels: client owns all work product upon creation, rather than waiting for full payment of fees.
Tougher on AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: the confidentiality obligation is one-way only, protecting the client but not AtliQ's own information.
Tougher on AtliQ than Crestline: five-year survival period for confidentiality instead of three years, and the obligations are not mutual.
Broadly like Trustline: same five-year survival period, but the obligations here protect the client's information only rather than being mutual.
Tougher on AtliQ than PayTrack: liability to the contractor is capped at 3 months of fees, and indemnity covers any loss from IP or confidentiality.
Tougher on AtliQ than Acme: one-way indemnity against AtliQ for confidentiality and misconduct, whereas Acme provided mutual indemnity for such claims.
Easier for AtliQ than Brightwater: liability to the contractor is capped at 3 months of fees, whereas the Brightwater cap was 150% of contract value.
Broadly like Orbit Travels: uses Indian law, but requires litigation in Pune courts instead of arbitration in New Delhi.
Tougher on AtliQ than PayTrack: disputes go directly to Pune courts instead of having a mandatory 30-day negotiation and arbitration process.
Easier for AtliQ than Brightwater: applies Indian law and Pune jurisdiction instead of English law and London courts.
